6.BLADDER PAIN SYNDROME
⇨Incidence 2.3 – 6.5%.
⇨Diagnosis by exclusion

pain, pressure or discomfort + urgency/ frequency/ nocturia/ persistent urge to void.

 

Over 6 weeks – 6months sometimes for years

With no identifiable cause.

History: RULE OUT

-UTI
-Calculi
-Pudendal nerve entrapment
-Radiation
-Drugs -ketamine
-Urethral diverticula
-Diverticular disease
-STI
-B outlet obstruction -Endometriosis
-Autoimmune -Prolapse
-IBS -OAB
-Vulvodynia. -Malignancy
-Vulvodynia -Bladder calculi
-Fibrinolysis. -Infection
-Chronic fatigue.

Pain:

-Location, type, relationship to bladder Filling and emptying.
-Triggering factors, onset.

Rule out Abuse:

Examination:

-Rule out Bladder distention.
-Hernia, trigger paints, prolapse.
-Vulval skin, bladder skin.
-Look for vulval, urethral, bladder tenderness

Investigations:

1.Bladder diary for 3 days, frequency volume chart
2.Food diary
3.Dip stick testing.
4.MSU –ve but patient is symptomatic – rule out Ureaplasma & Chlamydia.
5.Cytology –to rule out microscopic-hematuria.
6.Sterile-pyuria => acid fast bacilli.

 

 

1st line: @primary care

⇨Conservative T/m
-Analgesic.
-Relive Stress
-Dietary modification.
-Exercise.
-Support Group.

Failed

2nd line: @ secondary care.

⇨Medical t/m
-Oral Amitriptyline
-cimetidine
- gabapentin
- Pregabalin.

S/E:

-Dry mouth, sedation, constipation, wt gain.

 

Failed

MDT: Pain team + psychologist.

3rd line:

⇨intravesical.
-DMSO – dimethyl sulfoxide.
-Botulinum toxin A.
-Lidocaine.
-Chondroitin sulphate
-Hyaluronic acid.
-Heparin

Failed =>MDT

4th line: Neuromodulation.

-post tibial nerve or sacral nerve stimulation.
-Oral cyclosporine.

5th line @tertiary care level:

⇨Therapeutic cystoscopy
•Cystoscopy + Hydrodistension.
•Major surgery is considered

=>Total cystectomy + urinary diversion.

Huner lesion

-Reddish.
-Well demarcated.
-Bleed to touch.
-Need surgical treatment.
-ND – yag laser 88% cure.

Treatment Not Recommended:

-Antibiotics – Long term.
-Intravesical BCG
-I/V PPS.
-I/V long duration Hydrodistension.
-Oral glucocorticoid – Long Term.

Management Triage:

P0 Care: History Examination, investigations:

→DIP stick testing
→MSU
→DIARY.

+ conservative treatment for 3 – 6months.

Secondar care: after failed 1st line for 3 – 6m0.

Indication of MDT:

1. Refractory cases.

2. Before neuromodulation.

Follow – Up: In sec care till symptoms are controlled then in P0 care.

Tertiary care: Surgical treatment.

⇨Cystoscopy:
-to diagnose/ exclude other conditions.
-Biopsy to diagnose BPS ,Hunner lesions, glomerulation
⇨indications of Urodynamic:
-Not relieved by MedicationBPS + SI
-BPS + UI
-BPS + outflow obstruction

BPS on cytometry:

-Pain on filling
-Capacity.

-1st sensation to void.

BPS + OAB = 14%.

⇨BPS and Pregnancy:
-Effect of pregnancy on BPS – variable 7% improvement.
-Safe treatment – Amitriptyline and Intravesical heparin.
-DMSO – Teratogenic in animals.
-Sacral N stimulator – turn off.
